Subject: Draft DPA and carve-out for model training - Aurora Biotech

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. Attached is the redlined DPA (PDF) from our legal team. Our main outstanding concern is around the use of Customer Data for model training and improvement. We need explicit contractual language that Redwood will not use Aurora customer data to train or improve models that are redistributed or serve other customers.

Key asks from our side:
- A clear prohibition on using "Customer Data" for model training or producing model weights unless we provide an explicit, documented opt-in.
- A defined exception for aggregated, non-identifying telemetry used solely for service reliability/ops metrics, with a definition of "Aggregated Telemetry".
- Confirmation of subprocessors and a mechanism for prior notice/approval for sensitive subprocessors (e.g., model tuning partners).
- SCCs for EU transfers and a DocuSign path to execute the DPA.

I attached a redline with suggested language; Thomas (copied) will coordinate legal redlines. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the carve-out and we can move to signature.

Attachments: Aurora_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (redline PDF)

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Data Governance, Aurora Biotech

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aurorabiotech.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA and carve-out for model training - Aurora Biotech

Hi Laura — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're aligned with the principle that Customer Data should not be used to train models without explicit consent. A few clarifying points from our side so we can finalize the wording quickly:

- Definitions: We'll add explicit definitions for "Customer Data", "Model Training", "Aggregated Telemetry", and "De-identified Data". Our goal is to make the carve-out operationally precise (e.g., what counts as non-reversible de-identification).
- Allowed telemetry: We can accept a limited exception for Aggregated Telemetry that is non-identifiable, non-reversible, and only used for service reliability and capacity planning. We will not use Aggregate Telemetry to tune or change model weights used across other customers.
- Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a current subprocessor list and will provide SCCs for EU transfers. For subprocessors that might perform model tuning, we agree to a 30-day notice and the ability for Aurora to object on reasonable security/privacy grounds.
- Execution: happy to sign via DocuSign. I'll have legal circulate a final DPA for signature once we align on the exact language below.

Proposed high-level clause to include (draft):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models or model weights that are made available outside the Aurora account, except where Aurora provides an explicit, written opt-in. Redwood may use Aggregated Telemetry that has been irreversibly de-identified and cannot be associated with a Data Subject for the sole purpose of service reliability and performance monitoring; such Aggregated Telemetry shall not be used to produce or update model weights used to serve other customers."

I'll loop in Priya and Rishi to tighten the legal language and confirm SCC attachments. Can you confirm Aurora is comfortable with the wording above as a starting point?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: None (see Laura's redline)

Subject: Internal: Aurora DPA redline - proposed operational edits

Team — quick internal note after reviewing Laura's redline and Markus's response. I think we should accept the carve-out in principle but tighten the operational definitions so Aurora can't unintentionally block low-risk telemetry work that materially reduces costs (for both parties). Suggested edits:

- Define "Irreversibly De-identified" using a technical standard (e.g., k-anonymity threshold / removal of direct identifiers + cryptographic hashing with salt) and exclude hashed identifiers from model training unless opt-in.
- Add a clause that "Aggregated Telemetry" means metrics aggregated to at least the customer-account level and across a minimum time window so single-record leakage is impossible.
- Add a UI/contracting path: we can offer an "Account Training Opt-in" flag (recorded and auditable) so Aurora can opt-in per model if desired. This keeps the customer happy and preserves a straightforward product path.
- Subprocessors: propose Redwood's standard 30-day notice + curated list; for any subprocessor that will receive raw Customer Data for training activities, require prior written consent.

I attached a short internal mark-up of the redline (see Drive link in thread). If Rishi signs off on the definitions, I can present final wording to Laura and offer the DocuSign link for signature.

Attachments referenced: Aurora_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (internal mark-up stored on Drive)

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-05-12T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: Aurora DPA redline - proposed operational edits

Folks — reviewing the proposed language. I'm supportive with a few legal safeguards to avoid downstream risk:

1) Expand the prohibition to explicitly cover "derivative model weights" and any "model artifacts" (so we can't accidentally claim Aggregated Telemetry exemption to produce a shared embedding table that leaks customer patterns).
2) Add audit rights for Aurora limited to evidence of data handling for 12 months post-execution (log extracts, subprocessor attestations) — this is a reasonable ask and reduces future disputes.
3) For EU transfers, attach SCCs as an exhibit (Aurora_SCCs.pdf) and state Redwood's role and technical safeguards (encryption in transit, key management).
4) Subprocessor clause: for subprocessors that will perform any model tuning or receive Customer Data in raw form, require prior written consent. For other subprocessors (hosting, logging, telemetry analytics) keep 30-day notice.

I'll draft precise redline language for the DPA and circulate. For the "irreversibly de-identified" definition, legal prefers focusing on prohibitions (no re-identification, no reconstruction) and examples rather than a fixed technical threshold to avoid locking us into brittle definitions. Priya — can you confirm product can provide auditable opt-in flags and exportable logs for audit?

I'll prepare the final DPA for signature once we have Priya's confirmation.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final DPA language & DocuSign link (Aurora Biotech)

Laura — thanks for the patience. Attached is our final redline (we accepted the core carve-out). Below is the agreed, high-level clause we will include in the DPA (final redline PDF attached to the DocuSign envelope):

Agreed clause (summary):
- Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve models or model weights that are made available outside the Aurora account unless Aurora provides an explicit, documented opt-in.
- Redwood may use Aggregated, irreversibly de-identified telemetry for service reliability and performance monitoring only; such telemetry shall not be used to produce or update model weights used to serve other customers or to create derivative model artifacts.
- For subprocessors that will receive raw Customer Data for model-tuning activities, Redwood will obtain Aurora's prior written consent. For other subprocessors, Redwood will provide 30-day notice and maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list.
- SCCs attached in Exhibit A (Aurora_SCCs.pdf) govern EU transfers; Redwood will maintain encryption and KMS controls.
- Aurora will have limited audit rights (log excerpts and attestation) for 12 months post-execution to verify compliance with the training carve-out.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached final redline: Aurora_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (we updated definitions and added audit wording).
2) If this matches your expectation, please sign via DocuSign here: https://app.docusign.com/aurora/ds/12345 (envelope includes Aurora_DPA_redline_v3.pdf and Aurora_SCCs.pdf).
3) Once DocuSign completes, Redwood will: (a) mark the Aurora account with a "No-Training" flag by default; (b) provide the subprocessor list; (c) schedule a 30-minute handoff with Engineering to document telemetry aggregation and auditing procedures.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the final wording. Looking forward to getting this across the line.

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
